# Tracking domains
Source: https://lumail.io/docs/domains/click-domains.md

Tracked clicks, opens, the online version, and unsubscribe links need a host that is not your From domain. A **custom tracking domain** is the durable fix: recipients see your brand, and a blocklist hit on Lumail's shared fallback cannot take your mail down.

<DocsTella
  src="https://www.tella.tv/video/vid_cmtqt2u5j007q0agm9qtxgecv/embed?b=0&title=0&a=1&loop=0&t=0&muted=0&wt=0"
  title="How to set up a custom tracking domain"
/>

## What a tracking domain does

A tracking domain is the hostname Lumail uses for the links it adds to an email:

- Tracked links first open `/r/...`, record the click, then redirect to the original destination.
- The invisible open-tracking pixel loads from `/o/...` when open tracking is enabled.
- The online version loads from `/e/...`.
- Unsubscribe links use the same hostname.

Without a custom domain, Lumail provides a per-organization hostname on its [shared tracking domain](/docs/domains/click-domains-shared). Using your own verified web domain keeps these links recognizable and aligns them with the domain you already send from.

## Set up a custom tracking domain

### 1. Add a web domain

Open **Domains**, find **Web domains**, and click **Add web domain**. Use a dedicated subdomain such as `click.yourdomain.com` or `links.yourdomain.com`.

![Add a web domain for click tracking](/docs/domains/click-domain-add-web-domain.png)

Your tracking domain is also a web domain, so it can continue serving capture pages on the same host.

### 2. Configure DNS and wait for HTTPS

Add the CNAME record shown by Lumail to your DNS provider. Keep the TTL on **Auto** when that option is available.

Return to Lumail and click **Check DNS records**. The domain is ready when DNS, the certificate, and HTTPS are all verified.

![Verified CNAME and HTTPS for a Lumail web domain](/docs/domains/click-domain-dns-verification.png)

DNS propagation is not instant. If the record is correct but still pending, wait a few minutes and check again. See [Web domains](/docs/domains/web-domains) for Cloudflare and SSL troubleshooting.

### 3. Select the domain

Open **Settings → Configuration → Tracking domains**. Choose the verified web domain.

![Select a verified web domain for tracked links](/docs/domains/click-domain-select-domain.png)

The selected host is used for new tracked links, opens, online versions, and unsubscribe URLs. Capture pages already using that web domain are unchanged.

### 4. Test a tracked link

Send a test email containing a normal link. Open the message and inspect or click the link:

1. The URL should start with your custom hostname, for example `https://click.yourdomain.com/r/...`.
2. Opening it should redirect to the original destination.
3. The click should appear in the email or campaign analytics.

Already-sent emails keep their original tracking hostname and continue to work.

## Switch back to shared tracking

Open **Settings → Configuration → Tracking domains** and choose **Lumail shared tracking**. Only newly generated links switch back to the shared hostname.

Read [Tracking domains: Shared](/docs/domains/click-domains-shared) to understand how the fallback works and what changes when you use it.

## Quick checklist

- The web domain is verified.
- HTTPS is ready.
- The domain is selected in **Settings → Configuration → Tracking domains**.
- A test email uses your hostname and redirects correctly.
- The hostname is not blocklisted.

---

# Tracking domains: Shared
Source: https://lumail.io/docs/domains/click-domains-shared.md

A tracking domain is the hostname used for tracked links, open pixels, online email versions, and unsubscribe URLs. When you have not selected a custom tracking domain, Lumail provides one automatically through its **shared tracking domain**.

There is nothing to configure. Every organization receives its own stable hostname on Lumail's current shared tracking zone.

## What recipients see

A normal destination such as:

```text
https://yourwebsite.com/pricing
```

is represented in the email by a tracked URL similar to:

```text
https://a1b2c3d4e5.shared-zone.example/r/link-id
```

The ten-character label identifies the organization inside Lumail's tracking system. It is derived from the organization's stable ID, not its editable slug, so renaming an organization does not break previously sent links.

The exact shared zone can change as Lumail maintains its tracking infrastructure. Previously sent links remain served on their original hostname.

## What happens when someone clicks

```text
Recipient clicks the tracked URL
            ↓
Lumail receives /r/link-id
            ↓
The click is attached to the email and subscriber
            ↓
Lumail redirects to the original destination
```

The shared domain does not replace or modify the destination website. It provides the short redirect step needed to measure the click before the browser continues to the original URL.

## What uses the tracking domain

| Path              | Purpose                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/r/...`          | Records a tracked link click and redirects to its destination |
| `/o/...`          | Loads the open-tracking pixel when open tracking is enabled   |
| `/e/...`          | Opens the hosted online version of an email                   |
| `/unsubscribe...` | Processes the recipient's unsubscribe request                 |

All four use the same selected origin: your custom tracking domain when one is active, otherwise your shared Lumail hostname.

## Why each organization gets its own hostname

Lumail does not mint every organization's links on one identical hostname. The per-organization label provides host-level separation and allows Lumail to attribute traffic or investigate unusual activity without relying on an organization slug that can change.

This is useful isolation, but it is not the same as owning the registrable domain. Reputation systems can still evaluate the shared parent domain and affect every organization beneath it.

## Shared versus custom

|                          | Shared tracking domain             | Custom tracking domain                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Setup                    | Automatic                          | Requires a verified web domain and CNAME      |
| Visible brand            | Lumail-managed hostname            | Your hostname, such as `click.yourdomain.com` |
| Organization isolation   | Separate per-organization hostname | Fully separate hostname under your domain     |
| Parent-domain reputation | Shared with other Lumail customers | Aligned with your own domain                  |
| Existing links           | Continue working after you switch  | Continue working if you switch back           |

The shared option is useful while getting started and prevents tracking from being blocked by missing DNS setup. A custom tracking domain is recommended before sending at meaningful volume because recipients see your brand and you control the parent domain's reputation.

## Switch to your own domain

1. Add and verify a web domain such as `click.yourdomain.com`.
2. Open **Settings → Configuration → Tracking domains**.
3. Select the verified domain.
4. Send a test email and verify that its tracked links use your hostname.

Follow the visual [custom tracking domain tutorial](/docs/domains/click-domains) for the video, screenshots, DNS setup, and final verification.

## Switch back to shared

In **Settings → Configuration → Tracking domains**, choose **Lumail shared tracking**. Newly generated links use the shared per-organization hostname again. Already-sent links keep their original hostname and remain valid.

## What the shared domain does not do

- It does not change the destination behind a link.
- It does not bypass consent, unsubscribe, or deliverability requirements.
- It does not make every open reliable; inbox privacy features and image blocking can affect open tracking.
- It does not isolate the reputation of the shared parent domain as strongly as a custom domain.

Treat clicks as a useful engagement signal, not proof that a human read the entire email. Security scanners and inbox providers can also visit links automatically.

# Domains Overview
Source: https://lumail.io/docs/domains.md

Lumail.io uses two types of domains to power your email marketing:

## [Email Domains](/docs/domains/email-domains)

Send emails from your own domain (e.g., `hello@yourdomain.com`) instead of a shared domain. This improves deliverability and brand trust.

## [Web Domains](/docs/domains/web-domains)

Serve your capture pages on a custom domain (e.g., `pages.yourdomain.com`) for a seamless brand experience.

## [Tracking domains](/docs/domains/click-domains)

Reuse a verified web domain for tracked clicks, opens, and unsubscribe links. This is the real reputation fix; the shared Lumail fallback is only for orgs that have not set one.

## Domain Limits

Your plan determines how many domains you can add. Both email and web domains count toward your total domain limit.

| Plan     | Domain Limit |
| -------- | ------------ |
| Free     | 1            |
| Premium  | 5            |
| Business | Unlimited    |
